subject: MSA + Order Form: refine 'Grace-to-Cancel' window and mutual exit mechanics
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, James Li <james.li@cumulus-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form: refine 'Grace-to-Cancel' window and mutual exit mechanics

Hi team,

Attaching a cleaned-up redline of the MSA + Order Form (MSA_redline_v3.docx) with the specific asks Cumulus sent overnight. Quick summary of the open items I want cross-functional input on before we send back: 

- Auto-renew notice: Cumulus has asked for a 30-day notice for annual auto-renew. Our standard is 60 days; legal prefers 90 for large deals. Can we agree on a middle path?
- Short-cycle pilots: they want a 14-day "Grace-to-Cancel" window for pilots under $50k — ops says that risks load from churn.
- Termination for convenience: they request the right with 30 days' notice and a cap on pre-paid credits refund only. Legal wants explicit cap on liabilities and pro-rata refund.

Ask: Ben / Karthik — can you each propose one alternate clause (short, track-changes friendly) that addresses these three items? If we can converge on wording today I will route to Legal for redline sign-off and then back to Cumulus.

I flagged precedent language we use in mid-market (precedent_clause_DB.xlsx) and included an OF term summary (OF_term_summary.pdf).

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Manager, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai
Attachment: MSA_redline_v3.docx (document, 78KB)
Attachment: OF_term_summary.pdf (summary, 12KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, James Li <james.li@cumulus-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: refine 'Grace-to-Cancel' window and mutual exit mechanics

Priya — thanks for pulling this together. High level thoughts from Commercial: 

1) Auto-renew notice: propose we offer 60 days for annual terms and 30 days for 1-year pilots only if they commit to a 30% prepay. Wording suggestion (short): 
"Either party may terminate by providing written notice at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current Term; for Pilot Orders with aggregate committed spend <= $50,000, the notice period may be 30 days provided Customer has paid at least thirty percent (30%) of the Pilot Fees in advance."

2) Grace-to-Cancel: operational risk on 14 days — recommend 30 days for pilots, but allow 14 for free trials only.

3) TFC (Termination for Convenience): accept mutual right, but forgo automatic refunds beyond unused prepaid credits. Recommend pro-rata refund plus liability cap equal to 3 months' average fees.

I'll paste a one-liner redline for each into the doc and flag for Legal. If Karthik can confirm the liability cap language is OK from a risk perspective, we can knit this together.

-Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-30T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: refine 'Grace-to-Cancel' window and mutual exit mechanics

Thanks — I reviewed Ben's proposals and ran the precedent DB. A couple of notes from Legal: 

- 60 days for annual auto-renew is defensible. For pilots, we can allow 30 days without additional prepay if the Order Form explicitly disclaims reliance on long-term commitments (i.e., pilot-specific OF language). That reduces our exposure operationally.
- Grace-to-Cancel: 14 days is too short to unwind sessions and billing in our infra; suggest 21 days as a compromise for paid pilots.
- TFC: we must keep a liability cap and a pro-rata refund for prepaid fees; the proposed "3 months' average fee" cap is acceptable, but include a bright-line calculation clause: "Cap on Liability = greater of (i) three times the then-current monthly subscription fees; or (ii) total fees paid in the preceding three months."

I attached the precedent spreadsheet with clause IDs flagged (precedent_clause_DB.xlsx).

I will take the consolidated language and prepare a legal-approved redline this afternoon. Priya — once you have Ben's final OF tweaks, ping me and I'll produce a short memo to include with the return redline (helps procurement).

Regards,
Karthik

Priya / Ben / Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the clear options. We can land on 60 days for annuals, and Cumulus is willing to accept a 30-day notice for pilots if we confirm the "no reliance on long-term commitments" language in the OF. For the Grace-to-Cancel window, 21 days is acceptable. For TFC, the cap phrasing James Li (Procurement) approves the bright-line calculation proposed by Karthik.

Please send the updated redline and a DocuSign link once Legal signs off; we have a procurement checkpoint scheduled next Wed and would like to close before then.

Thanks — James
